rationale: C6 fusion already uses object_id as the candidate identity

evidence_id is a post-retrieval/evidence occurrence identity, not a safe cross-pass candidate identity
global_candidate_identity.evidence_id_role: OCCURRENCE/OUTPUT PROVENANCE ONLY — preserved per pass occurrence (stage_s_evidence_ids, CandidateOccurrence.evidence_id); never used to deduplicate or identify global candidates

pass_origins.semantics: provenance role only; implies no ranking priority; the contract separates pass origin from relevance rank by construction (no cross-pass rank fields exist)

fields: query_text (the query actually consumed by Retriever for this pass)
retrieval_plan (the complete RetrievalPlan used by the pass)
channel_candidates (executed channel, object_id, 1-based channel rank, optional channel-local score)
stage_r_order (reranker output order; may cover a Stage-F subset by design)
payloads (PayloadProvenance for every candidate in the pass universe)
pass_snapshot_schema.stage_terminology: F/R/M/P/S reused with their existing C6/C7 meanings; not redefined

fields: channel_occurrences (channel name + channel rank + optional channel score)
candidate_occurrence_schema.independence_rule: initial and targeted ranks are never collapsed into one number, never averaged, and neither pass is authoritative

global_pool_schema.behavior: consumes initial + targeted pass snapshots and produces ONE object-level candidate record per object_id
global_candidate_fields: payload (canonical PayloadProvenance; for BOTH-origin objects the identical-by-validation payload with INITIAL preferred deterministically)
payload_provenance_fields: text or payload_ref (stable reference sufficient for later reranking)

targeted_trigger_context_schema.semantics: provenance only; errors are not reinterpreted as answer points; E3 decomposition is NOT implemented
targeted_trigger_context_schema.pairing_rule: a targeted pass snapshot requires its TargetedTriggerContext and vice versa

required_complete_state_semantics.COMPLETE: stage_f_order membership equals the full channel-candidate universe AND stage_m_order/stage_p_order cover the same universe
required_complete_state_semantics.PARTIAL: any truncated/absent state; must carry non-empty completeness_notes
required_complete_state_semantics.anti_silent_truncation_rule: declaring COMPLETE with a truncated Stage-F/M/P order fails validation; the current production top-30 diagnostic output is PARTIAL, never the complete candidate universe
required_complete_state_semantics.current_production_bundle_can_populate: PARTIAL only (A0 finding); a later capture task populates COMPLETE state
required_complete_state_semantics.adapter_policy: no adapter from the current incomplete bundle to COMPLETE state was written in A1 (contract-first)

channel_provenance_rules.rule: channels record only streams actually executed by the pass; computed query representations with separate shadow methods are rejected as executed channels

version_provenance_invariants: every channel candidate has a non-empty object_id and rank >= 1; no duplicate (channel, object_id) entries
Stage-R IDs belong to Stage-F candidate membership
Stage-M membership equals deduplicated R+F membership; Stage-P membership equals Stage-M membership; no duplicate entries in F/R/M/P
Stage-S selected IDs and stage_s_evidence_ids keys belong to the pass candidate universe
stage_f_scores cover exactly the stage_f_order membership
every candidate in the pass universe has payload provenance (source_id, source_version_id, and text or payload_ref)
the same object_id cannot silently map to different source_id/source_version_id across passes (clear ValueError; no silent combination of versions)
origin BOTH requires both pass occurrences (guaranteed by construction and validated counts)

deterministic_serialization_contract.hash_ceremony: none; no new file-content hashes introduced
